title: Rapid growth of primary pulmonary meningioma with hemoptysis
case_prompt:
A 60-year-old woman presented with a 2-day history of cough and hemoptysis. She had well-controlled diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia and was a lifelong non-smoker. On examination, she was afebrile, SpO2 was 97% on room air, and there were no adventitious lung or heart sounds. Laboratory tests showed a leukocyte count of 11,700 cells/μl (80.2% neutrophils), C-reactive protein 2.22 mg/dl, and hemoglobin A1c 6.5%. Liver and renal function were normal. Serum carcinoembryonic antigen, cytokeratin-19 fragment, pro-gastrin-releasing peptide, β-D-glucan, aspergillus antigen, and cryptococcus antigen were within normal limits. An interferon-γ release assay for tuberculosis was negative. 

Chest radiography and contrast-enhanced CT revealed a non-enhanced, oval, well-circumscribed 5 × 6 × 10 cm mass in the right lower lobe, containing air bubbles and surrounded by a ground-glass halo. Review of a chest radiograph from one year earlier identified a 1-cm right hilum nodule. PET/CT showed no FDG uptake in the lesion. Bronchoscopy on hospital day 7 demonstrated active bleeding from the superior segmental bronchus of the right lower lobe without visible endobronchial lesions; lavage fluid cytology and bacterial cultures were negative, and biopsy was not obtained. 

Clinical differential diagnoses included lung cancer, rare benign hemorrhagic neoplasms, lung abscess, mycetoma, and congenital malformations such as congenital cystic adenomatoid malformation and bronchopulmonary sequestration.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Lung cancer — “Positron emission tomography/CT imaging showed no pathological accumulation of 18-fluoro-2-deoxy-D-glucose … in the mass.”  
2. Rare benign hemorrhagic neoplasms — “These benign tumors typically exhibit a slow growth rate, and they are symptomatic.”  
3. Lung abscess — “The cytology and bacterial culture of the bronchial lavage fluid had negative results.”  
4. Mycetoma — “Serum levels of β-D-glucan, aspergillus antigen, and cryptococcus antigen titer were also normal.”  
5. Congenital malformations — “Chest X-ray and contrast-enhanced computed tomography … revealed a non-enhanced, oval-shaped, well-circumscribed solitary mass measuring 5 × 6 × 10 cm in the right lower lobe.”
